contexts.text: [BASELINE] Canonical task wording.
As a homeowner, pick the smallest possible set of smoke detector models so that every room contains a model from your selection.
As a librarian, minimize the number of subject tags kept so that every reading list includes a tag drawn from your kept tags.
As an event planner, choose the fewest musicians necessary so that every party lineup features at least a musician you booked.
As an IT administrator, keep the selection of installed software as small as possible such that every user group has access to a package from that selection.
As a teacher, compile the tiniest collection of core books so that every course syllabus lists a book from your collection.
As a chef, limit pantry staples to the smallest variety so that every recipe on the menu uses an ingredient you stock.
As a gardener, reduce planted species to the minimum needed so that each garden bed contains a species you planted.
As an emergency planner, assign the minimal variety of vehicle types so that every neighborhood has a vehicle type available from your assignments.
As a fashion buyer, pare down the color palette to the least number of hues so that every outfit display incorporates a color from the palette.
As a store purchaser, select the fewest suppliers possible so that every product category on the shelf includes an item supplied by your chosen suppliers.
As a festival organizer, book the smallest number of headline acts so that each stage lineup contains an act you have secured.
As a photographer, pack the minimum set of lenses so that every kind of shoot you accept can be handled with a lens you brought.
As a casting director, hire as small a roster of actors as you can so that each role category includes an actor from your hires.
As a security manager, issue the fewest master access cards necessary so that every secured area can be opened with a card from your issued set.
As a mechanic, stock the smallest assortment of spare parts so that each common repair can be completed using a part you have on hand.
As a parent, buy the least variety of snacks so that every child finds a snack they like among the options you purchased.
As a travel agent, purchase the minimum number of attraction tickets so that every tour itinerary contains an attraction covered by your purchases.
As a museum curator, choose the fewest artworks to display so that each themed gallery contains a piece from your display selection.
As a volunteer coordinator, recruit the smallest team possible so that every task has a volunteer capable of performing it drawn from your recruits.
As a wedding planner, order the least variety of flower types so that each bouquet design incorporates a type from your order.
As a librarian, pick as few descriptive keywords as possible so that every book on the shelf is matched by at least one chosen keyword.
As an IT administrator, choose the smallest possible set of monitoring agents to deploy so that every application is observed by at least one selected agent.
As a school administrator, select as few teachers as possible to assign so that every student club has at least one appointed supervisor.
As a farmer, decide on the minimal number of fertilizer types to buy so that each field receives at least one of the chosen types.
As an event planner, select the smallest assortment of menu items so that every guest dietary preference is satisfied by at least one chosen dish.
As a warehouse manager, choose the minimal variety of pallet types so that every outbound shipment can use at least one selected pallet type.
As a parent, choose the fewest toys needed so that every child has at least one toy they like from the selection.
As a restaurant manager, select the smallest set of ingredients to stock so that every menu dish contains at least one stocked ingredient.
As a journalist, choose the fewest experts to interview so that every topic you plan to cover has at least one selected expert available.
As a theatre director, pick the minimal roster of understudies so that every principal role has at least one understudy who can cover it.
As a museum curator, select as few multilingual guides as possible so that every visitor language is supported by at least one chosen guide.
As a city planner, choose the smallest number of streetlight positions to install so that each crosswalk is illuminated by at least one selected light.
As a pharmacist, decide on the minimum set of medications to stock so that each common symptom category can be treated by at least one stocked medicine.
As a security manager, choose the fewest badge profiles to issue so that every secured door is accessible by at least one selected badge profile.
As a marketing manager, select as few influencers as possible so that every target demographic is reached by at least one chosen influencer.
As a gardener, choose the smallest variety of plants to cultivate so that each local pollinator species finds at least one attractive plant among those you plant.
As a data center engineer, select the minimal assortment of maintenance tools to keep on hand so that every likely failure type can be handled by at least one chosen tool.
As a software developer, choose the fewest plugins to include so that every project requirement is addressed by at least one selected plugin.
As a homeowner, choose the smallest possible set of tools such that every repair category has a selected tool available.
Assign the minimum number of students to present so that every project topic is represented by a presenting student.
Pick as few books as possible for the front display so that each genre has a featured title among the chosen books.
Pick the smallest set of security measures that ensures each vulnerability category is addressed by a chosen measure.
Select the fewest possible product lines so that every customer segment has a chosen item available.
Order the minimum number of diagnostic tests so that each symptom cluster is covered by a chosen test.
Pack as few items as possible while making sure each planned activity has a packed item to use.
Choose the smallest pool of peer reviewers so that every submitted manuscript has a selected reviewer who can assess it.
Pick the fewest shooting locations so that every type of subject can be photographed at a chosen location.
Choose as few songs as possible for the setlist so that each target audience mood is represented by a chosen track.
Buy the fewest toys necessary so that each of the pet's play styles is met by a purchased toy.
Assemble the smallest emergency kit that still ensures each potential scenario has a relevant item included.
Select the minimum set of vocabulary words so that every lesson topic contains a chosen word to teach.
Purchase the smallest assortment of communal supplies so that every team has a purchased item that meets its basic need.
Pick as few films as possible for the program so that every audience interest category has a chosen film screening.
Recruit the fewest volunteers needed so that every listed task is covered by a recruited volunteer with the required skill.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct smoke detector models available in the universe of choices; this counts every model type you could pick to standardize across the house.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of rooms that must each be covered by at least one chosen detector model; each room represents a constraint that needs to be 'hit' by your selection.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier (name or number) for a specific room in the house (e.g., 'kitchen', 'bedroom2'); used to refer to that room's acceptable models.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: A space-separated list of detector model identifiers that are acceptable for the given room; your chosen set of models must include at least one model from this list for the room to be considered covered.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct subject tags available in the library’s tag universe — i.e., how many different tags exist that you may choose to keep.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The number of reading lists that must each be covered — each reading list must contain at least one of the subject tags you decide to keep.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for a single reading list (used to reference this specific list in the collection of lists).

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: The space-separated subject tags that label this reading list; the kept tag set must intersect this list’s tags so the list is considered covered.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct musicians in the universe of possible hires — the size of the pool of people you can book. Used to know how many unique musician IDs or names exist.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of scheduled weekend parties (lineups) that each must include at least one musician you hire. This is the count of constraints you must cover.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for a specific party lineup (e.g., a number or label). Each party_id names one event that must be covered by at least one booked musician.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated identifiers (names or numeric IDs) of the musicians performing on that party's bill. You must hire at least one of these musicians to claim presence at this party.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct software packages in the universe from which the administrator may choose installations. Each element corresponds to one package identifier.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of user groups that must be covered. Each set represents a user group that needs at least one compatible package installed.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for a user group (the set). Use this to refer to which group the following compatible packages belong to.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated package identifiers that are compatible with this user group. The chosen install list must include at least one of these for the corresponding user_group_id to be considered covered.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct book titles in the universe formed by all course syllabi — the complete pool of candidate core books you may select from.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of course syllabi (courses) that must each be represented by at least one chosen title on the shared reading list.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for this course syllabus (e.g., course code or index). It identifies which course must be 'hit' by selecting at least one title from its list.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: A space-separated list of book titles that appear on this specific course's syllabus; each listed title is a candidate to include in the shared reading list and will 'hit' this course if selected.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct ingredients in the kitchen universe (the count of different possible staples you might stock). Use this to understand the size of the ingredient pool from which staples are chosen.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of recipes (dishes) on the menu that each must be covered by at least one stocked staple. This is the number of constraints the pantry selection must hit.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for a single recipe (a dish index or name). Each recipe_id labels one menu item that must be covered by stocking at least one of its ingredients.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated ingredient tokens used in this recipe. Each token names an ingredient from the kitchen universe; selecting any one of these for the pantry will 'cover' this recipe. Tokens are treated as distinct ingredient identifiers.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct plant species present across the allotment (the universe of species you may choose to keep). This counts unique species once and is the pool from which you select a minimal set to retain.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of garden beds that must each contain at least one of the species you decide to keep. Each bed represents a constraint that must be 'hit' by selecting a species present in that bed.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for a specific garden bed (for example a name or number). Use this to refer to which bed the listed species belong to.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated list of plant species currently planted in this bed. Choosing any one of these species counts as covering (hitting) this bed; species names are identifiers and duplicates across beds are allowed but count once toward the kept species.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct vehicle types in the universe (the pool of different vehicle kinds you may choose from). This counts unique types — duplicates are not separately counted.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of neighborhoods that must each be served by at least one chosen vehicle type. Each neighborhood corresponds to a set that must be 'hit'.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for a neighborhood (for example a name or index). This labels the constraint that requires at least one assigned vehicle type.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated list of vehicle types that are available/acceptable for this neighborhood. Choosing any one of these types will satisfy (hit) this neighborhood's requirement.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of candidate hues available to choose from for the pared-down palette. Use this to understand the universe of colors you may select.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of outfit displays on the floor that each must show at least one of the chosen palette colors.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for a single outfit display (e.g., label or index). Refer to this when ensuring each outfit is covered by the selected palette.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: A space-separated list of the color names (hues) present in this outfit display. Each listed color is a candidate from the universe; the chosen palette must include at least one color from this list for the outfit to be considered 'hit'.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total count of distinct suppliers available to hire (the universe of supplier choices). This is an integer describing how large the supplier pool is; supplier identifiers themselves appear in the category records.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The number of shelf product categories that must each be covered by at least one chosen supplier. Each category is a constraint that your supplier team must 'hit'.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for a single shelf product category (for example '1', 'C1', or a short label). Each such category must have at least one product supplied by someone on your selected supplier team.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated supplier identifiers (IDs or short names) who supply items in this category. Choosing any one of these suppliers will satisfy coverage for this category. Supplier identifiers may repeat across categories; selecting the same supplier for multiple categories only counts once toward headcount.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct headline acts available across all stage lineups (the size of the universe of acts you may book). This counts each act once even if they appear on multiple stage rosters.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of stages (each stage is a set that must be 'hit' by booking at least one act that appears on its lineup).

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for a specific stage (e.g., Stage1, MainStage). Each stage must have at least one of the booked headline acts from its lineup.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated act identifiers or names listed on this stage's lineup. These are the candidate acts that, if booked, will cover this stage. An act appearing on multiple stage_lineup_acts only counts once toward the total hires.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct lens options in the universe the photographer can choose from (count of unique lens models/IDs that might be packed).

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The number of different shoot types on the calendar that must each be covered (each is a constraint that requires at least one suitable lens).

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for one shoot type/constraint (e.g., 'wedding', 'portrait', or a numeric id) that must be hit by bringing at least one compatible lens.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated identifiers of lenses (from the universe of distinct lenses) that are suitable for this shoot type — at least one of these lenses must be packed to cover the shoot.

global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct available performers in the casting pool (the universe of actors you can hire). This counts every actor identifier that may appear in the role lists.

global_fields.scenario_description: The number of role categories that must each be covered by your hires (the number of constraints/sets). Each category must have at least one hired actor who can perform it.

item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for a role category that needs to be filled (e.g., a name or numeric id). This labels the constraint that at least one actor able to play this role must be hired.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated actor identifiers (names or IDs) who are able to perform this role category. Hiring any one of these listed actors satisfies (hits) this role. Each token corresponds to an actor from the total_actors universe.

global_fields.scenario_description: The total count of distinct master access cards in the pool that could be issued. This is the universe size from which you will choose a minimal subset to cover every secured area.

global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of secured areas (each must be opened by at least one issued card). This is the number of constraints that your chosen cards must collectively satisfy.

item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for a single secured area (e.g., 'Lobby', 'ServerRoom1'). Use this to refer to the area whose access must be covered by at least one issued card.

item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated identifiers of master cards that can open this secured area. When choosing which cards to issue, at least one of these listed cards must be selected to cover this area.

item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for a specific themed gallery (one constraint to hit). Use this ID to refer to the gallery that needs at least one artwork from your chosen display.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated identifiers of artworks that are on displayable in this gallery. Each token is an artwork from the museum inventory; selecting any one of these for the overall display will satisfy this gallery's requirement. The same artwork identifier may appear in multiple gallery lists.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct volunteer candidates available to recruit (the size of the universe of elements). This tells you how many unique volunteer identifiers may appear across all tasks.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of tasks that must each have at least one recruited volunteer assigned (the number of sets that must be 'hit').

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A label or identifier for this specific task. Each task represents a constraint that needs at least one of the recruited volunteers who appear in its eligible_volunteers list.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated identifiers of volunteers who are capable of performing this task. A valid recruit list must include at least one of these identifiers for every task.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct flower varieties available to choose from — the size of the universe of flower types you may order.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of different bouquet designs that must each include at least one flower type from your order.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for a single bouquet design (e.g., a label or index). Use this to refer to that particular design when deciding coverage.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: A space-separated list of the flower type labels (names or IDs) that appear in this bouquet design. Ordering any one of these types will 'hit' (cover) that bouquet.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct descriptive keywords in the universe that you may choose from; this is the size of the keyword pool the librarian can pick.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of books on the shelf; each book represents a constraint that must be matched by at least one chosen keyword.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for this book (e.g., an index or short label) used to reference the book whose descriptions (keywords) follow.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: A space-separated list of descriptive keywords that apply to this book; selecting any one of these keywords will 'hit' (cover) the book.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct monitoring agents available to deploy — the size of the universe of agent choices from which solutions pick agents.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of applications/services that must each be monitored at least once; each application represents a constraint (a set) that must be 'hit' by selecting at least one compatible agent.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for this application/service (e.g., a name or numeric ID). This labels the constraint that needs coverage and ties the listed agents to that specific application.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated agent identifiers that are capable of monitoring this application. Choosing any one of these agents will cover (hit) the application; agent IDs refer to entries in the universe of available agents.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct teachers available to be assigned as supervisors (size of the teacher pool/universe). This number counts each teacher once even if they can supervise multiple clubs.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of student clubs that must each have at least one appointed supervisor. Each club represents a constraint that must be covered by selecting at least one teacher.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for a student club (e.g., a name or numeric ID). Each record with this ID describes which teachers can supervise that specific club.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: A space-separated list of teacher identifiers who are able or assigned to supervise the given club. Selecting any one of these teachers will cover (hit) that club.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total count of distinct fertilizer types available on the market (the universe of elements). Use this to know how many different fertilizer IDs/types exist in the instance.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The number of fields on the farm that must each receive at least one chosen fertilizer type. Each of these corresponds to a constraint that must be covered.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for a specific field (e.g., 'Field1' or an index). This labels the constraint that the chosen fertilizers must cover.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: A space-separated list of fertilizer type identifiers that can be applied to this field. The field is covered if at least one of these listed fertilizer types is purchased.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct dishes available to choose from — the universe of menu items the planner can select. Count each dish once; these are the elements you may pick to build the smallest menu.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of guest dietary preferences or constraint groups that must each be satisfied. Each preference corresponds to a set of acceptable dishes and must have at least one dish chosen for it.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for this dietary preference or guest constraint (e.g., a preference label or guest ID). It names the set that must be 'hit' by selecting at least one acceptable dish.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated list of dish identifiers or names that satisfy this dietary preference. The final menu must include at least one dish from this list to cover the corresponding preference.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct pallet types in the warehouse (the universe of elements). Each element corresponds to one pallet type you may choose; the objective is to pick as few distinct pallet types as possible.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of outbound shipments/truckloads that must each be served. Each shipment is a constraint that must be 'hit' by selecting at least one pallet type usable for that shipment.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for a specific outbound shipment (e.g., a shipment number). Used to reference which shipment the listed pallet types apply to.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated identifiers of pallet types that are usable for this shipment. Selecting any one of these pallet types will cover (hit) the corresponding shipment; repeating the same pallet type across shipments is redundant.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct toy types available to choose from. This is the size of the universe of toys you may bring; the goal is to select as few of these toy types as possible while still giving every child at least one toy they like.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of children who must each be given at least one toy they like. Each child corresponds to a set (a list of toys they approve), and every one of these children must be covered by the chosen toys.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for a specific child (for example 'child1' or a name). This labels the child whose preferences are given on this line; you must ensure the selected toys include at least one from this child's liked list.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated toy identifiers that this child likes. Choosing any one of these toy types will satisfy this child; the same toy identifier may appear in multiple children's lists and counts only once toward the total toys brought.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct ingredients in the universe of possible pantry items — i.e., how many different ingredient types exist across all dishes and could be chosen to stock.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The number of dishes on the menu. Each dish is a constraint that must be covered by at least one stocked ingredient.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier or name for a single menu dish (for example a dish number or title) used to refer to that dish in the list of constraints.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: A space-separated list of ingredient names that appear in this dish. If any one of these ingredients is stocked in the pantry, this dish is considered covered (hit).

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct experts available to choose from. Expert identifiers used elsewhere (in experts_for_topic) refer to these individuals.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of topics the journalist must cover. Each topic must be assigned at least one selected expert.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for a single topic that must be covered (e.g., a number or short label). Each topic corresponds to one constraint that must be 'hit' by selecting an expert who appears for that topic.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated expert identifiers who can speak to this topic. Selecting any one of these experts will cover (hit) the topic. Identifiers must refer to the pool counted by total_experts.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct understudy candidates in the pool (the universe of people you may hire). This tells you how many unique people exist to choose from when building the minimal roster.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of principal roles that need coverage. Each role is a constraint that must have at least one of the chosen understudies capable of stepping in.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier or name for a principal role (e.g., the character name or an index). Each such ID denotes one role that must be covered by at least one hired understudy.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: A space-separated list of understudy identifiers (names or IDs) from the candidate pool who can cover this principal role. Hiring any one of these people will satisfy coverage for the role; identifiers must refer to entries in the available understudies universe.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of available multilingual guides (the universe of selectable elements). This is how many distinct guide IDs exist to choose from.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of visitor languages that must be covered (each is a constraint/set that must be 'hit' by selecting at least one guide who speaks it).

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (name or code) of a visitor language that must be supported by the team of guides.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated identifiers of guides who speak this language — i.e., the guide IDs that can cover this language if selected.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of candidate lamp-post positions on the neighborhood map (the universe of possible lights you may choose from).

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of crosswalks that must each be illuminated by at least one selected lamp-post position (each is a constraint to be 'hit').

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: The unique identifier for a single crosswalk (one constraint). Use this id to reference which crosswalk the following list of positions can illuminate.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated identifiers of lamp-post positions that can illuminate this crosswalk. Selecting any one of these positions will light the crosswalk.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct medicines in the available universe — i.e., how many different medication options exist to choose from when building the pharmacist's stocking list.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of common symptom categories that must each have at least one treatment available on the shelf; each corresponds to a constraint that must be 'hit' by stocking at least one medication that treats it.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for a single symptom category (a complaint or condition). Use this id to refer to the category that needs at least one stocked medicine.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated list of medicine names or identifiers that can treat the given symptom category. These are the candidate medicines that, if stocked, will cover (hit) this category.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct badge profiles available to issue in the building — the universe of profile identifiers you may choose from. This is a count of unique profiles; duplicates are not extra.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of secured doors that must each be covered by at least one selected badge profile. Each set corresponds to a single door (a constraint to be hit).

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for a secured door (the set being covered). Use this id to refer to the door when checking coverage by selected badge profiles.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated badge profile identifiers that can open this door. Each token is a profile from the universe; the door is covered if at least one of the chosen distinct profiles appears here. Treat repeated profile ids as the same profile.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct influencer candidates available in the roster — the universe size from which you will choose a minimal crew.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of target demographic groups that must each be reached by at least one selected influencer.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier (label or index) for a specific target demographic group; used to reference which audience must be covered.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated identifiers of influencers who reach this demographic. Selecting any one of these influencer IDs counts as covering the demographic.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct plant varieties available in the universe — i.e., how many different plant types you could potentially choose for the garden.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of local pollinator species that must each find at least one attractive plant among those you plant.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for one pollinator species (for example 'P1', 'P2', etc.). Each such identifier labels a constraint that must be covered by at least one planted variety.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated labels of the plant varieties that attract this pollinator species. Planting any one of these varieties will satisfy (hit) this pollinator's requirement.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct maintenance tool types in the universe (each is a selectable tool type that could be kept in the cabinet). This counts tool types, not duplicates, and gives the size of the universe you may choose from.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of likely failure types or outage scenarios that must each be handled by at least one chosen tool. Each represents a constraint that the selected tool assortment must 'hit'.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier or label for a specific failure type/outage scenario (e.g., a short name or numeric id). This names the constraint that must be covered by at least one tool in the chosen assortment.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated list of tool type identifiers that can handle this failure type. Selecting any one of these tools covers (hits) the failure. Tool identifiers correspond to the universe of available tool types.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct plugins in the toolbox (the universe of selectable plugins). Use this to know how many unique plugin IDs exist overall.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The number of project requirements that must each be addressed by at least one chosen plugin (i.e., how many constraints/sets must be hit).

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier (name or index) for a single project requirement; used to reference which requirement the following plugins can satisfy.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated plugin identifiers from the toolbox that can each satisfy this requirement. Treat each token as a plugin you may select; selecting any one of them 'hits' the requirement.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct tool types available in the home tool universe. Treat this as the size of the pool of different tools you may choose from to place on the workbench.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of repair categories (each is a constraint) that must be covered. Each category requires at least one selected tool that can handle that kind of repair.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: An identifier for a specific repair category (e.g., a name like 'plumbing' or a numeric id). It labels one constraint that must be 'hit' by selecting at least one suitable tool.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated names of tools that can address this repair category. Selecting any one of these tools on the workbench satisfies the corresponding repair category; tool names refer to items in the overall tool universe and duplicates do not provide extra coverage.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of students in the universe of possible presenters — i.e., how many distinct students signed up overall (each is an available element you may choose to present).

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct project topics that must each be represented by at least one presenting student.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: An identifier for a single project topic (e.g., a topic code, number, or short name). This labels the constraint that at least one student presenting this topic must be chosen.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: A space-separated list of student identifiers (names or IDs) who signed up to present that topic. Selecting any one of these students will cover (hit) this topic; each student may be chosen at most once.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct book titles in the universe of candidates for the front display. This counts each title once (even if it appears in multiple genres) and gives the solver an idea of how many unique books may be chosen.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of genres that must each be featured on the display. Each genre corresponds to one constraint/set that requires at least one chosen title to represent it.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for a single genre (e.g., an index or short genre name). This labels the constraint that at least one of the listed candidate titles must be selected to represent that genre.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated list of book titles or book IDs that belong to this genre. Choosing any one of these titles will cover (hit) the genre. A title may appear in multiple genre lists, allowing one selected book to represent several genres; selections must be unique (no duplicate copies of the same title).

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct security measures in the universe — how many different measures the team may choose from. Use this to understand the universe size when minimizing the chosen measures.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of vulnerability categories (constraints) that must each be addressed. A valid solution must cover every one of these categories.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for a single vulnerability category (a constraint). This label names the bucket that must be hit by selecting at least one associated measure.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated identifiers of security measures (from the universe) that mitigate this vulnerability category. The chosen solution must include at least one of these measures for the corresponding category to be covered.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct product lines in the catalog universe — the pool of items you may choose from. This number counts unique product-line identifiers and defines the domain of selectable items.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of customer segments that must each be served. Each segment represents a constraint that requires at least one chosen product line to be available for that segment.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for a customer segment (e.g., a label or index). Used to reference the segment whose needs are described by the corresponding product-line list.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated identifiers of product lines that satisfy this customer segment. Each listed product line must come from the product-line universe; at least one of these must be selected to serve the segment. Treat repeated identifiers as a single product line (no double-counting).

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct diagnostic tests in the drawer (the universe of elements you may choose from). This tells the solver how many different test IDs exist overall.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of symptom clusters (constraints) that must each be covered by at least one chosen test. Each cluster corresponds to a set that must be 'hit'.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for a single symptom cluster (the set). Use this ID to refer to which cluster is being described; every cluster must have at least one chosen test that covers it.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated list of test IDs (from the drawer) that check this symptom cluster. A chosen solution must include at least one of these tests for the cluster to be considered covered; tests are distinct and selecting a test counts once.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct packable items available to choose from (size of the universe of items you may bring).

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of planned activities that each require at least one packed item to cover.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for a specific planned activity (e.g., an index or short label) that must have at least one matching packed item.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated list of the items (by name or id) that can be used for this activity; packing any one of these items will satisfy that activity.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct reviewers in the available pool (the universe of reviewer IDs you may choose from). This counts each reviewer once and defines the domain from which you must pick the smallest reviewer team.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of submitted manuscripts that must each be assigned at least one of the chosen reviewers. Each manuscript corresponds to one constraint that must be 'hit' by the selected reviewer team.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for a single submitted manuscript (e.g., an index or code). Use this to reference which submission the following reviewer list applies to.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated reviewer identifiers (from the available reviewer pool) who are capable of reviewing the given manuscript. To cover this manuscript, at least one of these reviewers must be included in the selected minimal reviewer team; repeated names have no extra effect.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct shooting locations the photographer can choose from (the universe of possible stops).

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The number of different subject types that must each be photographed at least once (each is a constraint that must be 'hit').

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier/name for a subject type (e.g., a particular species, scene, or portrait category) that must be photographed.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: A space-separated list of location identifiers where this subject type can be photographed — choosing any one of these locations will satisfy the requirement for that subject.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct candidate tracks in the band's pool (the universe of songs you may choose from). Used to understand the range of song identifiers.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The number of distinct audience moods that must each be represented at least once in the final setlist; each corresponds to one constraint/set to be hit.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier (name or index) for a specific target audience mood that needs representation in the setlist.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: A space-separated list of song identifiers from the available pool that are considered to represent this mood; choosing any one of these tracks will satisfy (hit) the mood.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct toy options in the universe — i.e., how many different toys exist that you could potentially buy. This counts unique toy identifiers; buying duplicates of the same toy does not increase coverage.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The number of the pet's play styles that must each be satisfied. Each play style is a requirement that must be 'hit' by at least one purchased toy.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (name or index) of a single pet play style requirement. This labels the constraint that needs to be covered by buying toys.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: A space-separated list of toy identifiers (names or IDs) that satisfy this play style. Purchasing any one of these listed toys will cover the corresponding play style; the list elements are drawn from the universe of toys.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct candidate items available to choose from for the emergency kit (the universe size). This counts each item type once and corresponds to how many different item names appear across all scenarios.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The number of different potential situations or scenarios that the kit must cover. Each scenario is a constraint that must contain at least one item you pack.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for a specific potential situation (e.g., 'S1', 'hike_cold', or a numeric id). Use this to refer to which scenario the listed items are meant to help.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: A space-separated list of candidate item names that would be useful for this scenario. When you choose items for the kit, at least one of the names in this list must be included to 'hit' (cover) this scenario.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct vocabulary words available in the universe from which we may choose. Use this to know the size of the pool of candidate words for the curriculum.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of lesson topics that must each be covered (i.e., each must contain at least one chosen vocabulary word). This is the count of constraints the chosen word list must hit.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for a single lesson topic (e.g., an index or label like 'Lesson1'). Each lesson must be matched by at least one chosen vocabulary word.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: The vocabulary words that appear in this lesson, given as space-separated tokens. A valid curriculum selection must include at least one of these words for this lesson to be considered covered.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total count of distinct communal product types in the universe from which purchases may be made. This is the size of the product-type list that the co-op can choose items from.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of activity groups (teams) that need at least one purchased item they can use. Each team corresponds to one constraint that must be 'hit' by selecting at least one acceptable product type.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for a particular team or activity group. Use this ID to refer to the group whose needs are described on this line.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: A space-separated list of product-type identifiers that this team finds acceptable. The co-op must purchase at least one product type from this list to satisfy that team's basic need.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct films in the pool you may choose from for the program. This counts every film once and defines the universe of selectable titles.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The number of different audience interest categories that must be covered (e.g., documentaries, teen viewers, animation lovers). Each of these is a constraint that requires at least one chosen film appealing to that interest.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: An identifier for one audience interest category (a constraint). This labels which interest the following list of films can satisfy.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: A space-separated list of film identifiers (from the available pool) that would appeal to this interest category. Choosing any one of these films will 'hit' (cover) the corresponding interest.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct volunteers available in the roster (the universe size). This tells the solver how many individual people can potentially be recruited; each selected volunteer counts once toward the objective.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of tasks/jobs that must be covered. Each task corresponds to a constraint that must be 'hit' by recruiting at least one volunteer who has the required skill.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for a single task/job that needs coverage (e.g., Task1, T3). Use this to refer to which job the following list of volunteers can cover.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: A space-separated list of volunteer identifiers who are qualified to perform the given task. For each task_id, at least one of these volunteers must be recruited to cover that task.
